'''RailTel Corporation of India Limited (RCIL)''' is an Indian Navaratna [[Public Sector Undertakings in India|Public Sector Undertaking]] (PSU) which provides [[broadband]] and [[VPN]] services. RailTel was formed in September-2000 with the objective of creating a nationwide broadband, telecom and multimedia network, and to modernise train control operation and safety system of [[Indian Railways]]. RailTel's network passes through around 5,000 stations across the country, covering all major commercial centres.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=100106 |title=RailTel Celebrates its Annual Day|date=18 October 2013 |publisher=Press Information Bureau, Indian government|access-date=4 April 2014}}</ref> RailTel became the 22nd company to achieve Navratna status on 30-August-2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 September 2024 |title=Railtel secures Navratna Status from GoI |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/railtel-sjvn-nhpc-bag-navratna-status-from-finmin-shares-in-focus-12811789.html |access-date=3 September 2024 |website=Moneycontrol}}</ref>

==History==
The Indian Railways (IR) was initially solely dependent on the Department of Telecom (now [[BSNL]]) for their control and administrative communication circuits. To increase circuit efficiency, the Railways began building up its own communication systems from early 1970s based on overhead telephone lines, [[quad cables]] and [[microwave]] signalling. In 1983, the Railway Reforms Committee decided to introduce [[optical fibre cable]] (OFC) based communications in IR to provide safety, reliability, availability and serviceability through use of a dedicated network. The decision was also taken to create a network independent of the DoT and replace the existing microwave telecom systems (60% of which had reached end of life) with OFC.

Indian Railways commissioned the first OFC on the [[Western line (Mumbai Suburban Railway)|Churchgate–Virar line]] in Mumbai in 1988 for train operation and control purpose, which consisted of 60 km of network across 28 stations. The network was expanded in Central India with the commissioning of 900 km of OFC network in 1991–92 across Durg–Nagpur, Nagpur–Itarsi and Itarsi–Bhusaval sections of the [[Howrah–Nagpur–Mumbai line]], and in Eastern India with the commissioning of 60 km of OFC network in [[Tatanagar–Bilaspur section|Tatanagar–Chakradhrapur section]] of the same line.

The second National Telecom Policy in 1999 opened the National Long-Distance segment under favourable licensing conditions with revenue sharing to assist mobile network operators to spread their networks across India. In 2000, the Government announced the formation of a telecom corporation to build a nationwide broadband multimedia telecommunication network. RailTel was established on 26-September-2000 as a [[Public Sector Undertaking]] (PSU), wholly owned by the Indian Railways.<ref>[http://www.railtelindia.com/profile/about-us.html Rural Broadband Connectivity Provider in India | RailTel<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

===WiFi and WiMax===
RailTel, formerly in collaboration with [[Google]], provides free [[WiFi]] Internet access at selected railway stations across India. Google chose railway stations as the location to provide free WiFi because stations have access to a reliable power supply and [[Fiber-optic communication|fibre]] provided by RailTel, and because the passengers at a station come from all demographics of India.<ref>{{cite web|title=Google teams up with RailTel to give free Wifi to all railway stations in India|url=http://www.indialivetoday.com/google-teams-up-with-railtel-to-give-free-wifi-to-all-railway-stations-in-india/16505.html|website=India Live Today|access-date=25 August 2016|date=30 July 2016|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828042322/http://www.indialivetoday.com/google-teams-up-with-railtel-to-give-free-wifi-to-all-railway-stations-in-india/16505.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The free WiFi service was launched at [[Mumbai Central railway station]] in January-2016.<ref>[http://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/mumbai/mumbai-central-gets-googles-highspeed-wifi-network/article8140702.ece Mumbai Central gets Google's Wi-Fi network – The Hindu<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> In April-2016, the service was expanded to nine more railway stations.<ref>{{cite news|title=Google, RailTel expand free WiFi reach, cover 9 more stations|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/google-railtel-expand-free-wifi-reach-cover-9-more-stations-116041500438_1.html|newspaper=[[Business Standard]]|access-date=17 April 2016}}</ref> In June-2016, Google announced that free WiFi was available at 19 stations in India and was being used by over 1.5 million people.<ref>{{cite web|title=1.5 million Indians enjoy high Speed Wi-Fi across 19 Railway Stations|url=https://india.googleblog.com/2016/06/15-million-indians-enjoy-high-speed-wi.html?m=1|website=Official Google India Blog|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref>

In September-2016, Google announced a public WiFi initiative called [[Google Station]]. The company planned to expand free WiFi coverage under the initiative to locations such as cafes and malls across India, and later expand worldwide.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Byford|first1=Sam|title=Google Station is a new platform that aims to make public Wi-Fi better|url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/9/27/13070922/google-station-public-wi-fi-india|website=The Verge|access-date=28 September 2016|date=27 September 2016}}</ref>

In June-2018, Google announced that its Free WiFi project was now running at 400 Indian railway stations. As a result, there were more than 8 million people accessing the internet each month via the project.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/transportation/railways/google-says-free-wifi-available-at-400-railway-stations/articleshow/64492865.cms|title=Free WiFi Service: Google's free WiFi now available at 400 Indian Railways stations|newspaper=The Economic Times}}</ref>

The partnership between Google and RailWire ended in May-2020. Now RailWire alone provides free WiFi for 30mins at low speed and further paid plans at 34 Mbps to more than 5000 railway stations in India.<ref>{{cite news| url = https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/google-ends-its-free-wifi-service-at-indian-railway-stations/article30878776.ece| title = Google ends its free WiFi service at Indian railway stations - The Hindu| website = [[The Hindu]]| date = 21 February 2020}}</ref>

===RailWire<ref>{{Cite web|title=RailWire - RailTel's Express Network|url=https://www.railwire.co.in/}}</ref>===
Based on its nationwide fibre network, RailTel offers RailWire, a joint venture with [[managed service provider]]s to provide internet, voice, video and multimedia access on a single FTTH connection at a customer's home or office.<ref>{{cite news|title=RailTel to tie up with MSOs to expand internet base in rural T.N.|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/tamil-nadu/railtel-to-tie-up-with-msos-to-expand-internet-base-in-rural-tn/article5387079.ece|newspaper=The Hindu|date=25 November 2013|location=Chennai, India}}</ref>


==Awards==
RailTel received the 12th National Awards for Excellence in Cost Management 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Railway PSU – "RailTel" Bags 12th National Awards for Excellence in Cost Management 2014|url=http://pib.nic.in/newsite/PrintRelease.aspx?relid=123344|access-date=19 July 2015|publisher=Press Information Bureau of India}}</ref>
